bills.title: AI Communications Privilege
bills.summary: Would treat AI communications as legally privileged professional communications.

bills.title: Chatbot Disclosures for Minor Users
bills.summary: Would require disclosures for minor users of 'conversational AI services.'

bills.title: Companion Chatbot Crisis Intervention Requirements
bills.summary: Would require companion chatbots to implement structured interventions, including a 20-minute pause and referral to human crisis support, when detecting credible expressions of self-harm or harm to others, and mandates annual reporting.

bills.title: Employer AI Notice and Workplace Surveillance Disclosure
bills.summary: Would require employers to provide detailed written notice and annual updates to workers about the use of AI tools in employment decisions and workplace surveillance.

bills.title: Surveillance Data and Automated Systems Pricing/Wage Prohibition
bills.summary: Would prohibit the use of surveillance data and automated decision systems to set individualized prices or wages.

bills.title: AI in Health Care (Illinois HB 1806-style)
bills.summary: Modeled on Illinois' HB 1806; would regulate the use of artificial intelligence in health care settings.

bills.title: Hawaii AI-Generated Music Streaming Ban
bills.summary: Would ban music streaming that is performed or attributed to an AI music artist.
bills.status_detail: Deferred in committee and is unlikely to advance this session absent further action

bills.title: Iowa Chatbot Disclosure Requirements
bills.summary: Would establish disclosure requirements for chatbots (not minor-specific). Passed through the Senate Technology Committee.
bills.status_detail: Passed through the Senate Technology Committee

bills.title: Iowa Chatbot Safety Bill
bills.summary: Iowa chatbot safety and disclosure bill.

bills.title: Iowa Data-Driven Pricing Regulation (HF 2469)
bills.summary: Iowa data-driven pricing regulation bill.

bills.title: Iowa Data-Driven Pricing Regulation (SF 2278)
bills.summary: Iowa data-driven pricing regulation bill.

bills.title: Indiana Conversational AI Disclosure and Minor Protections
bills.summary: Would establish disclosure, safety, and content requirements for public-facing conversational AI services, with enhanced protections for minors.
bills.status_detail: Introduced by the Senate Committee on State Affairs

bills.title: Kentucky AI Companion Platform Parental Consent and Obligations
bills.summary: Would impose obligations on AI companion platforms, including verifiable parental consent and prohibition of relationship-forming AI (PRA).

bills.title: Kentucky AI in Health Care (Illinois HB 1806-style)
bills.summary: Modeled on Illinois' HB 1806; would regulate artificial intelligence in health care settings.

bills.title: Kentucky Mental Health Chatbot Privacy and Safety Requirements
bills.summary: Would create strict privacy, transparency, and safety requirements for mental health chatbots in Kentucky, mandating clear disclosures and limiting data sharing.

bills.title: Louisiana Prohibition on Harmful Material to Minors via Interactive Computer Services
bills.summary: Would prohibit interactive computer services from delivering or algorithmically promoting material harmful to minors to minor users.

bills.title: Maryland Algorithmic Consumer Reporting Agency Anti-Bias Requirements
bills.summary: Would impose strict transparency, accuracy, and anti-bias requirements on consumer reporting agencies that use algorithmic systems, mandating human oversight, regular audits, and consumer opt-out options.

bills.title: Maryland AI-Enabled Toy Child Safety and Privacy Requirements
bills.summary: Would establish stringent child safety, data privacy, and oversight requirements for AI-enabled toys, mandating parental controls, transparency, and prohibiting inappropriate, manipulative, or harmful content.

bills.title: Maryland Chatbot Regulation Bill
bills.summary: Maryland chatbot regulation bill.

bills.title: Maryland Data-Driven Pricing Regulation
bills.summary: Maryland data-driven pricing regulation bill.

bills.title: Mississippi Statutory Definition of Artificial Intelligence
bills.summary: Would set a definition for artificial intelligence in Mississippi code, largely modeled on the OECD's AI definition.

bills.title: Oregon AI Companion Disclosure and Safety Protocols
bills.summary: Would require AI companions to disclose AI interactions and implement safety protocols. Passed through committee.

bills.title: Pennsylvania AI Chatbot Minor Protection and Safety Requirements
bills.summary: Would establish strict age verification, content restrictions, and data security requirements for AI chatbots to protect minors from harmful content and ensure responsible use.

bills.title: Rhode Island Healthcare AI Documentation Disclosure Requirement
bills.summary: Would require healthcare providers and facilities to notify patients whenever artificial intelligence is used to document their in-person or telehealth visits.

bills.title: Rhode Island AI and Automated Decision Systems in Employment
bills.summary: Would establish strict regulations on the use of AI, automated decision systems, and electronic monitoring in employment, prioritizing worker privacy, transparency, anti-discrimination, and meaningful human oversight.

bills.title: Tennessee Coercive Suicide via AI Offense
bills.summary: Would create a new 'coercive suicide' felony offense for owners of an AI system that encourage or advise users to commit suicide.

bills.title: Tennessee Prohibition on Advertising AI as Mental Health Professional
bills.summary: Would prohibit the advertising of an AI system as a mental health professional.

bills.title: Utah AI Regulatory Sandbox and Mitigation Agreements
bills.summary: Amends Utah's existing regulatory sandbox (SB 149, 2024) by expanding the program to allow applicants to apply for a regulatory mitigation agreement or a joint interpretation agreement clarifying the application of state law to AI. Directs the Office of AI Policy to perform regular audits and allows up to two extensions on agreements. Also amends the Artificial Intelligence Learning Laboratory Program.
bills.status_detail: Passed out of the House and heads to the Senate

bills.title: Utah Generative AI Provenance Data Requirements
bills.summary: Would establish provenance data requirements for generative AI content.

bills.title: Utah Frontier Model Safety Plans and Whistleblower Protections
bills.summary: Would require frontier AI developers to publish safety and child protection plans and establish whistleblower protections. The White House urged Utah lawmakers to reconsider this bill, stating it is inconsistent with the administration's broader AI policy agenda.
bills.status_detail: White House urged Utah lawmakers to reconsider; Administration stated opposition as inconsistent with federal AI policy agenda

bills.title: Virginia AI Safety Independent Verification Organizations Licensing
bills.summary: Would establish a state licensing framework for independent verification organizations (IVOs) that assess whether AI systems meet defined safety and risk-mitigation standards. The Virginia CIO would oversee licensing, set independence and transparency requirements, and coordinate with an Artificial Intelligence Safety Advisory Council. Licensed IVOs would evaluate developers' governance practices and risk controls. Requires annual public reporting.

bills.title: Virginia Chatbot Duty of Loyalty and Emotional Dependence Detection
bills.summary: Would require covered chatbot operators (with more than 500,000 monthly active users) to detect and mitigate user 'emotional dependence,' prohibit human misrepresentation, and mandate crisis interventions when users show signs of self-harm. Requires notification to emergency services within 24 hours if a user faces imminent risk of death or serious physical injury. Includes a private right of action.

bills.title: Washington Chatbot Minor Protections
bills.summary: Companion bill to SB 5984 following a California SB 243-style companion chatbot framework with additional requirements. Operators must provide recurring disclosures every three hours that a chatbot is not human, implement heightened protections when the operator knows a user is a minor or when the chatbot is directed to minors, prohibit manipulative engagement practices for minors, and implement protocols to detect and respond to suicidal ideation.

bills.title: Washington Chatbot Minor Protections (SB 5984)
bills.summary: Companion bill to HB 2225 following a California SB 243-style companion chatbot framework with additional requirements. Operators must provide recurring disclosures every three hours that a chatbot is not human, implement heightened protections when the operator knows a user is a minor or when the chatbot is directed to minors, prohibit manipulative engagement practices for minors including excessive praise, simulated romantic relationships, and encouraging minors to conceal interactions from parents. Operators must also implement protocols to detect and respond to suicidal ideation.

bills.title: Washington GenAI Provenance Detection Tool Requirement
bills.summary: Would require covered providers to make a provenance detection tool available to users. The tool must publicly return detected provenance data and be accessible via uploads, links, or API access without requiring users to visit the provider's website. Covered providers may not collect or retain personal information except under designated circumstances. Must give users the option to include a manifest disclosure indicating when image, audio, or video content was created or altered by the provider's generative AI system.

bills.title: Maryland AI Health and Liability Bill
bills.summary: Set to be heard on February 25 in both the House Health Committee and the House Judiciary Committee.
bills.status_detail: Set to be heard on Feb. 25 in the House Health Committee and House Judiciary Committee

bills.title: Nebraska Chatbot Bill
bills.summary: Set to be heard February 24 in the Banking and Commerce Committee.
bills.status_detail: Set to be heard Feb. 24 in the Banking and Commerce Committee

bills.title: Alabama App Store Accountability Act
bills.summary: Governor Ivey signed this App Store Accountability Act into law on February 17. Effective date January 1, 2027. Largely aligns with the ASAA laws passed in Texas, Utah, and Louisiana last year, but extends age verification and parental consent requirements to existing accounts, requires parental consent for pre-installed apps, removes application exemptions, and adopts a definition for 'in-app purchases.' Does not include a private right of action.
bills.status_detail: Signed by Governor Ivey on February 17, 2026; effective January 1, 2027

bills.title: California CCPA Consumer Rights Email Request Method
bills.summary: Would require a business that does not operate exclusively online to offer an email address for submitting consumer rights requests in addition to a telephone number.

bills.title: California Delete Act Amendment — 30-Day Deletion Compliance
bills.summary: Delete Act amendment that would require data brokers to comply with deletion requests within 30 days rather than 45.

bills.title: California CCPA Whistleblower Complaints
bills.summary: Would allow individuals to submit whistleblower complaints to CalPrivacy alleging violations of the CCPA, with the individual receiving 15-33% of the fine collected if certain criteria are met.

bills.title: California Digital Choice Act — AI and Social Media Data Portability
bills.summary: Would amend the CCPA to add obligations with respect to AI and social media, including requiring social media companies or persons deploying AI models to allow consumers to request copies of personal information, contextual data, and social graphs; and requiring model operators to implement third-party-accessible interoperability interfaces to allow users to share contextual data with other AI models.

bills.title: Kansas App Store Accountability Act Age Assurance Framework
bills.summary: Passed by the Kansas Senate on February 18 with amendments. Senate amendments include amending the definition of 'account holder' to require association with the device and creation of an app store account, adding a definition for in-app purchases limiting it to digital currency or goods purchases, clarifying the effective date as January 1, 2027, and removing the proposed private right of action. The bill now moves to the House for consideration.
bills.status_detail: Passed by the Senate on February 18, 2026 with amendments; moves to the House

bills.title: Kentucky Kids Code Amendment to Comprehensive Privacy Law
bills.summary: Would amend Kentucky's comprehensive privacy law to incorporate South Carolina and Nebraska design code-style protections for minors, including requiring high-level privacy and safety settings by default, providing tools allowing minors to opt-out of algorithmic recommendation systems, and providing parents with controls over minor accounts. Also establishes processing restrictions including prohibiting targeted advertising and dark patterns directed at minors.

bills.title: Kentucky App Store Accountability Act
bills.summary: Would establish an App Store Accountability Act framework aligning with the models enacted in Utah, Louisiana, and Texas in 2025.

bills.title: New Hampshire Comprehensive Privacy Law Amendment — Children's Location Data
bills.summary: Would amend the state's comprehensive privacy law to prohibit a controller from selling 'the location and other sensitive data regarding children.' The law currently defines 'personal data collected from a known child' as sensitive data.
bills.status_detail: New Hampshire House voted 214-145 to pass the amendment; bill has yet to pass the Senate

bills.title: Oklahoma Comprehensive Privacy Bill (Virginia-style)
bills.summary: Virginia-style comprehensive privacy bill. The House voted to amend and pass with a narrow amendment adding a new exemption for compliance with the federal Controlled Substances Act and pushing the effective date to January 1, 2027. The bill must return to the Senate for a concurrence vote.
bills.status_detail: House voted to amend and pass; bill returns to Senate for concurrence vote

bills.title: Oregon Data Broker Civil Law Enforcement Data Sale Restriction
bills.summary: Narrowed in committee from a broader prohibition to specifically prohibit a public body from disclosing personally identifiable information to a data broker unless the data broker provides a written attestation that the information will not be sold or transferred to any entity that will use the information to enforce federal immigration law.
bills.status_detail: Narrowed in committee; original broader prohibition amended to limit scope to immigration law enforcement data protection

bills.title: South Dakota App Store Accountability Act
bills.summary: The State Affairs committee passed this ASAA bill with amendments on February 18, including requiring app stores to prevent minors from downloading or purchasing a developer's app if requested by a developer, and clarifying that developers are not prohibited from allowing a parent to customize age-related restrictions, safety features, and settings.
bills.status_detail: State Affairs committee passed with amendments on February 18, 2026

bills.title: Utah ASAA Law Amendment
bills.summary: The House Economic Development and Workforce Services Committee passed this ASAA amendment with amendments on February 18, removing exceptions for developers of 'family account applications,' narrowing the 'significant changes' definition, adding new requirements for pre-installed apps and existing accounts, and clarifying that developers are not prohibited from allowing a parent to customize age-related restrictions. May impact ongoing CCIA lawsuit challenging the Act's constitutionality.
bills.status_detail: House Economic Development and Workforce Services Committee passed with amendments on February 18, 2026

bills.title: West Virginia Biometric Information Privacy Act
bills.summary: Would enact a Biometric Information Privacy Act (BIPA-style) regulating the collection, capture, purchase, retention, and use of biometric identifiers and biometric information by private entities.
